info.name: Ciro Fuel Delivery Platform API
info.description:
Multi-tenant B2B fuel delivery platform — REST API (`/api/v1`). Mirrors `specs/001-fuel-delivery-platform/contracts/rest-api.md` and `scripts/smoke.http`.

## How to run
1. Import the companion environment `ciro-fuel-local.postman_environment.json` (or edit the collection variables directly) and point `baseUrl` at your running server.
2. Make sure the platform owner is seeded: `npm run seed:super-admin` (uses `SUPER_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env`) — update the `superAdminEmail` / `superAdminPassword` variables to match.
3. Run the **Auth → Login – Super Admin** request first.
4. Run **Companies → Create Company** (`commercialRegister` is optional — attach a small PDF/image if you want to test it) — this seeds a Fuel Company Admin too. Then **Companies → Set Fuel Prices** (order creation 400s without it).
5. Run **Auth → Login – Fuel Admin**, then **Users → Create Client** and **Companies → Create Transporter** — a Transportation Company is a separate tenant, spec 004; a driver belongs to it, not to the fuel company.
6. Run **Companies → Assign Regions** so the transporter actually serves the client's region, or approval will park the order at `AWAITING_ROUTING` with no candidates. Then **Users → Create Driver** (under the transport company) and **Auth → Login – Transport Admin**.
7. Run **Auth → Login – Client** / **Auth → Login – Driver** — these sign in with `phone`, not email (see the note below).
8. spec 008 fleet setup, once per transporter: **Trucks → Create Truck** + **Pair NFC Card** (or **Mint QR Token**), and **Tanks → Create Tank**. **Warehouses → Create Warehouse** (SUPER_ADMIN) near the delivery coordinates you'll use — **Dispatch → Assign Driver** fails with `NO_WAREHOUSE_FOR_GRADE` without one that supplies the order's grade.
9. Walk the **Orders** folder top to bottom for the full lifecycle: create → approve → pay (**Payments → Webhook – Sadad**, if `DIRECT`) → **Dispatch → Get Candidates**/**Assign Driver** → **Verify Vehicle – Departure** → **Verify Vehicle – Loading (Geofenced)** → **Confirm Loading** → **Driver Arrive** → **Get Current OTP** (as CLIENT) → **Verify Arrival OTP** → **Request Delivery OTP** → **Get Current OTP** again → **Verify Delivery OTP**.

## Login identifiers
`POST /auth/login` takes **one** of two identifiers:

| Role | Identifier | Variable |
|------|-----------|----------|
| SUPER_ADMIN, COMPANY_ADMIN | `email` | `superAdminEmail`, `companyAdminEmail` |
| CLIENT, DRIVER | `phone` (E.164, e.g. `+9665XXXXXXX`) | `clientPhone`, `driverPhone` |

A CLIENT/DRIVER phone is unique platform-wide because it *is* their credential: creating or updating a user with a non-E.164 phone returns `400`, and reusing one returns `409`. Admin phones are never resolved by **this** endpoint, so sending an admin's phone here returns `401`.

### Admin phone login (spec 015)
Administrators (SUPER_ADMIN / FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN / TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN) can also sign in **passwordless, by phone**, via a separate two-step flow — email+password (above) still works too, this is an alternative, not a replacement:
1. **Auth → Login by Code – Request** (`POST /auth/login/code/request`) — always `202`, identical body whether the number resolves to an admin, a non-admin, or nobody at all (FR-015); a 6-digit code is SMS'd only when it resolves to exactly one active admin. Set `loginCodePhone` to that admin's E.164 number first (defaults to `companyAdminPhone`).
2. Read the code — from the real SMS, or from the no-op sender's log when `SMS_PROVIDER=none` — and put it in `loginCode`.
3. **Auth → Login by Code – Verify** (`POST /auth/login/code/verify`) — same token-pair shape as `POST /auth/login`; the test script routes the tokens into the right role-specific variables automatically.

After repeated requests for the same number, step 1 can start returning `400 CHALLENGE_REQUIRED` with a proof-of-work `{seed, difficultyBits}` instead of the `202` — expected under `LOGIN_POW_DIFFICULTY_BITS` > 0 (the local default); not handled by this collection, since solving it needs a small script, not a request. Set `LOGIN_POW_DIFFICULTY_BITS=0` in your local `.env` to skip it entirely while testing.

Each login request captures its token into a role-specific variable (`accessTokenSuperAdmin`, `accessTokenCompanyAdmin`, `accessTokenClient`, `accessTokenDriver`) plus a generic `accessToken`/`refreshToken` pair (whichever logged in most recently). Requests use the role-specific variable that actually owns that route, so folders can be run out of order as long as the relevant login already ran once.

Cross-tenant or wrong-role access returns `404`/`403` per `rest-api.md` — that's expected, not a bug, if you mix up which token a request uses.

request.description:
[public] 10/min. Requires the seeded platform owner (`npm run seed:super-admin`).

This endpoint takes **email** only — sending this account's phone here returns 401, since `POST /auth/login` resolves phone for CLIENT/DRIVER alone. To sign in by phone instead, use **Login by Code – Request/Verify** (spec 015) with `loginCodePhone` set to `superAdminPhone`.

[public] Run **Companies → Create Company** first so this account exists.

This endpoint takes **email** only — sending this account's phone here returns 401. To sign in by phone instead, use **Login by Code – Request/Verify** (spec 015); `loginCodePhone` already defaults to `companyAdminPhone`.

This is the FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN created alongside the Fuel Company (spec 004 — COMPANY_ADMIN's direct successor).

[public] Run **Companies → Create Transporter** first so this account exists.

TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN — owns a driver fleet, picks up orders routed to its company (spec 004 US2/US4). This endpoint takes **email** only; to sign in by phone instead, use **Login by Code – Request/Verify** (spec 015) with `loginCodePhone` set to `transportAdminPhone`.

[public] spec 015 US2 — step 1 of passwordless administrator sign-in (SUPER_ADMIN / FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN / TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN only; CLIENT/DRIVER never resolve here). 10/min.

Always `202` with the same body — admin, non-admin or unknown number, SMS sent or failed (FR-015) — so this response never confirms whether `loginCodePhone` belongs to anyone. A code is created and SMS'd only when it resolves to exactly one active administrator; read it from the real SMS or the no-op sender log (`SMS_PROVIDER=none`) and put it in `loginCode`, then run **Login by Code – Verify**.

After repeated requests for the same number this can instead return `400 CHALLENGE_REQUIRED` with a proof-of-work `{seed, difficultyBits}` body — not handled by this request (solving it needs a script); set `LOGIN_POW_DIFFICULTY_BITS=0` locally to avoid it while testing.

[public] spec 015 US2 — step 2. Run **Login by Code – Request** first and set `loginCode` to the 6-digit code it sent. Response is byte-identical in shape to `POST /auth/login` (FR-016); the test script below routes the returned tokens into whichever role-specific variable matches `user.role`.

Wrong, expired, superseded or attempt-locked-out code all return the same `400 LOGIN_CODE_INVALID` with no attempt count (FR-017).

CLIENT signs in with **phone**, not email — phone is the login identifier for CLIENT/DRIVER and must be E.164 (`+9665XXXXXXX`). Email is reserved for the SUPER_ADMIN / COMPANY_ADMIN dashboard logins. An admin phone is never resolved here, so it returns 401.
DRIVER signs in with **phone** (E.164), same rule as the client. Deactivated accounts and suspended companies return the same generic 401 as bad credentials.
[public] Rotates the generic `accessToken`/`refreshToken` pair (whichever role logged in most recently).
Current user profile for whichever role last logged in (`{{accessToken}}`).
[public] The 13 Saudi regions and their governorates (Arabic/English names) — reference data for `Company.servedRegions` and `User.station.regionCode` (spec 004 FR-010).

formdata.description: Optional. Any PDF/JPEG/PNG under 10MB — see files.constants.ts for the MIME allowlist. Leave unattached (or disable this field) to create the company without a commercial register file.

request.description: SUPER_ADMIN. Multipart. Creates the tenant + its first Company Admin in one call (FR-018). `commercialRegister` is optional — enable the field and select a file (e.g. `scripts/fixtures/sample-register.pdf`) to attach one, or leave it disabled to create the company without it.
SUPER_ADMIN.
SUPER_ADMIN, or that company's own COMPANY_ADMIN.
SUPER_ADMIN. `status` is `ACTIVE` or `SUSPENDED`. A suspended company's users get `401` on login/refresh.
Own COMPANY_ADMIN or own CLIENT.
Own COMPANY_ADMIN (FR-008a). Run this before creating orders so `estimatedPrice` can be computed.
FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (own company). Creates a `type: TRANSPORT` company under `:companyId` plus its TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN in one call (spec 004 US2). Run **Auth → Login – Fuel Admin** first.
FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (owning the transporter at `:id`). Replaces `servedRegions` wholesale — drives routing (spec 004 FR-014/FR-015/FR-016). Run **Companies → Create Transporter** first.

Any authenticated caller whose own company this is (`assertCompanyAccess`) — a CLIENT reads their own fuel company's configuration to price the quote screen; only a FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN may set it (spec 005 T053).

Returns `deliveryFee`, `serviceFeePercent`, `taxRatePercent` and `tankerCapacitiesLiters` — the ladder the client's quantity selector steps through (FR-017).

**409 `PRICING_NOT_CONFIGURED`** when the company has no configuration. FR-011j: an unconfigured company must fail loudly rather than return an empty body the client cannot distinguish from a malformed response.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. The single authority behind every itemised breakdown (spec 005 D3/FR-011f).

`tankerCapacitiesLiters` must be non-empty and **strictly ascending** — the client's quantity ladder is rendered in exactly this order (FR-017). It comes from the fuel company's own configuration, never from transport companies' `Truck.maxCapacityLiters`, which would cross a tenant boundary (FR-017a).

A change here never rewrites an order already priced (FR-011i).

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. `station{regionCode, governorateCode, location}` required for CLIENT accounts (spec 004 FR-010/FR-011) — `governorateCode` must belong to `regionCode` (see **Regions → List Regions**). `addressText`/`name` are optional (FR-013).

`phone` MUST be E.164 (`+9665XXXXXXX`) and is unique platform-wide for CLIENT/DRIVER because it is their login credential:
- non-E.164 → `400`
- already registered → `409`

After this runs, **Auth → Login – Client** can sign in with the same `{{clientPhone}}`.

TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN. `truck` required for DRIVER accounts — capabilities are denormalized onto the driver doc (R8). The fleet belongs exclusively to the transporter (spec 004 FR-004a's symmetric counterpart — a Fuel Company can no longer create drivers).

`phone` MUST be E.164 and unique platform-wide (it is the login credential): non-E.164 → `400`, already registered → `409`.

Run **Auth → Login – Transport Admin** first.

Negative case: reuses `{{clientPhone}}` with a fresh email. Phone is unique platform-wide for CLIENT/DRIVER, so this must return `409 Conflict` — it used to surface as a `500`. Run **Create Client** first.

exec: // Must not be a 500 — a duplicate credential is a client error.

query.description: CLIENT | DRIVER | COMPANY_ADMIN — omit or leave empty for all
true | false — omit or leave empty for all

request.description:
COMPANY_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN. Tenant-filtered automatically — a COMPANY_ADMIN only ever sees their own company's users.

Filters are optional and are enabled/disabled per param above. An empty value (`?role=`) counts as "no filter" rather than matching nothing.
COMPANY_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, or the user themself.

COMPANY_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, or self (limited fields). `role`/`companyId` are immutable — only `fullName`/`phone` are whitelisted.

`phone` is re-validated here exactly as on create (non-E.164 → `400`, already registered → `409`) because for a CLIENT/DRIVER it **is** the login credential — an unchecked edit would lock the account out.

The test below copies the new number into `clientPhone`, so **Auth → Login – Client** keeps working after this request rotates it.

exec: // Phone is the login identifier — keep Login – Client runnable after the rotation.

request.description: COMPANY_ADMIN.
COMPANY_ADMIN. Deactivating a driver mid-delivery blocks NEW assignments only — their active order still completes.
COMPANY_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, or self. Select an image for `file` before sending.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (own client). Sets the client's CREDIT-method ceiling (spec 004 FR-023) — available credit is always derived as `creditLimit − Σ(outstanding ISSUED credit invoices)`, never a separately mutated counter (FR-024a). Target must be a CLIENT.

CLIENT (spec 005 T081/US5). Returns `creditLimit`, `consumed` and `available`, computed live from the same calculation the order path uses to refuse an over-limit order — the dashboard and the credit screen therefore cannot disagree (FR-026).

`creditLimit: null` means no facility is assigned; the client is told so rather than shown a figure (FR-027). Nothing is stored (research R6).

CLIENT (spec 005 T097/US7). **202** once the code is dispatched by SMS to the **new** number — never the existing one, so possession of the new number is what gets proven (FR-035b).

The phone is *not* changed yet: it stays as it was until the code is confirmed, and an abandoned or expired verification leaves the original in force (FR-035c).

Throttled to **3 requests / 15 min per user** (429 with `retryAfterSeconds`). A number already registered elsewhere yields **409 `PHONE_IN_USE`** and no SMS is sent (FR-035e). A provider failure yields **502 `SMS_SEND_FAILED`** rather than a false 202 (FR-035f).

The code is never returned in any response, logged, or displayed (FR-035g) — read it from the SMS provider, or from the `SmsSender` no-op's log line when `SMS_PROVIDER=none`.
CLIENT. Exactly 6 digits. The change takes effect only on a correct code (FR-035). Hashed at rest, single-use, expiring, and limited to **5 attempts per code** — a locked-out attempt surfaces as 429.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (spec 005 T108). Every station registered to that client, including inactive ones.

Nested under `/users` because the client owns the set. `findById` is itself tenant-scoped, so a foreign or nonexistent id 404s before any station work happens.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. Registering a station is the fuel company's responsibility — a CLIENT can never create, rename or remove one (FR-036b), and the app offers no control implying otherwise.

A client may hold several (D2/FR-036); the first becomes the default. `governorateCode` must belong to `regionCode` or the call is a 400.

A newly registered station appears for the client without an app update (FR-036c).

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. Suggests an address for a dropped pin at client registration (spec 004 FR-011) — never final, never re-derived on a later read (FR-012/013). Never throws: a missing API key, network failure or empty result all return `{ addressText: '' }`. The only external address-lookup call in the platform — order reads never make one (SC-007).

CLIENT. 201 with `status: PENDING_APPROVAL` and computed `estimatedPrice` (FR-007/008a). Requires fuel prices to already be set for the company (**Companies → Set Fuel Prices**).

`deliveryLocation` is optional — omit it to fall back to the client's own station location, or pass raw coordinates directly (as here) to create an order with **no station at all**, e.g. for a one-off manual test. `paymentMethod` (spec 004 FR-021) is one of `DIRECT` (default — the client pays, via **Payments (Webhooks)**), `DEFERRED` (the Transportation Company pays) or `CREDIT` (drawn against `creditLimit` — see **Users → Set Credit Limit**).
Any role, scoped automatically: CLIENT→own, DRIVER→assigned, COMPANY_ADMIN→company, SUPER_ADMIN→all. Swap the bearer token to see each scope.

Includes `statusHistory`. Driver DTO never includes `otps`.

spec 008: also returns `truckId`/`tankSummary`/`warehouseSummary`/`verifications[]` once a driver is assigned — `verifications`/`tankSummary` are stripped for CLIENT (FR-042); every role instead sees `vehicleVerified` (true only for a genuine matched DEPARTURE verification, never an override — FR-047d).

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. Optional `{ finalPrice?, transportCompanyId? }` — omitted `finalPrice` ⇒ `finalPrice = estimatedPrice`. Issues the order's invoice using `finalPrice` (spec 004 FR-020) — a CREDIT order over the client's available credit is refused (400, no invoice issued, FR-025). A DIRECT order then goes to `PENDING_PAYMENT` (routing deferred until settlement, FR-020a); DEFERRED/CREDIT route immediately — one serving transporter ⇒ `ROUTED_TO_TRANSPORT`; none ⇒ `AWAITING_ROUTING` + notified (FR-016); several ⇒ `AWAITING_ROUTING` with `routingCandidates` in the response unless `transportCompanyId` was supplied (FR-014).

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. Resolves an `AWAITING_ROUTING` order manually (spec 004 FR-014's Fuel-Company choice among several candidates, or FR-016's later resolution once a transporter gains region coverage). `409` if the order isn't `AWAITING_ROUTING`; `400` if the choice doesn't actually serve the region.
COMPANY_ADMIN. Alternate path from `PENDING_APPROVAL` — only run this against a fresh order that hasn't already been approved (409 otherwise).
CLIENT (while PENDING_APPROVAL/APPROVED/PENDING_PAYMENT) or COMPANY_ADMIN (until IN_TRANSIT). Releases the driver and clears any payment-timeout job transactionally (FR-009).
COMPANY_ADMIN, or CLIENT (blocked once `paymentTimeoutCount >= 2`, FR-015a). Only valid from `APPROVED` after a payment timeout.
CLIENT (order owner) only. The ONLY route where plaintext OTP appears (FR-021/022). Run after **Driver Arrive** or **Request Delivery OTP**.

spec 008 US3 (5/15min throttled). One endpoint for both stages — which one is derived from the order's own status, never from the request (research R7). At `ASSIGNED_TO_DRIVER` this is the DEPARTURE check: on match, advances to `LOADING` and returns `warehouseSummary` — that's the next destination (FR-026). `method` is `NFC_CARD` or `QR_CODE` (use `{{qrToken}}` as the credential for the latter). `403 VEHICLE_MISMATCH` — deliberately the SAME code whether the credential is wrong or simply unknown (Principle II).

spec 008 US4 amendment (2026-08-27, research R14). Same card, second read — but at `LOADING` this additionally requires the driver to be within `WAREHOUSE_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_METERS` (default 500m) of the assigned warehouse. `driverLocation` here should match the warehouse you created (or the one **Assign Driver** picked automatically) to pass.

`403 VEHICLE_MISMATCH` — wrong truck, answered first, reveals nothing about location. `403 NOT_AT_WAREHOUSE` — right truck, outside the radius; body carries `distanceMeters`/`radiusMeters`. `400 LOCATION_REQUIRED` — no `driverLocation` at all; nothing is recorded, since nothing about the vehicle could be evaluated. A successful match here does NOT itself advance the order — run **Confirm Loading** next.

spec 008 US4. Empty body — no quantity field exists anywhere in this flow (FR-028); the authoritative volume arrives later from an Aramco invoice, a separate feature. Requires the LOADING-stage verification above to have already matched — `409 VEHICLE_NOT_VERIFIED` otherwise. On success, `LOADING → IN_TRANSIT` and the delivery is routed to the customer.
DRIVER (assigned). Order must be IN_TRANSIT. Generates the ARRIVAL OTP; response contains no OTP. Idempotent while an unused, unexpired OTP exists.
DRIVER (assigned). Throttled 5/15min. On match → UNLOADING; 422 wrong OTP; 429 throttled (FR-021/023). Run **Get Current OTP** first to populate `{{currentOtp}}`.
DRIVER (assigned). Order must be UNLOADING. Response contains no OTP — fetch it via **Get Current OTP** as the client.
DRIVER (assigned). Throttled 5/15min. On match → DELIVERED (transaction), driver released (FR-022). Run **Get Current OTP** again first — the delivery OTP replaces the arrival one.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN only (403 for DRIVER/CLIENT). Order must be `LOADING`, `IN_TRANSIT` or `UNLOADING` (409 otherwise — spec 008 FR-046e added `LOADING` to the set, so an operator can still short-circuit a delivery stuck at the depot). `reason` is 5–500 chars and required. Marks `statusHistory` with `manualOverride: true` (FR-025).

CLIENT (spec 005 T054/US2). Returns the itemised `breakdown`, an opaque `quoteToken` and `expiresAt`.

The four components — `fuelLineTotal`, `deliveryFee`, `serviceFee`, `tax` — always reconcile to `total` (FR-011b). The app never computes or apportions any of them itself.

`stationId` must be the caller's own; a foreign id 404s without revealing whether it exists. Run **Stations → List My Stations** first to populate `{{stationId}}`.

Pair the saved `{{quoteToken}}` with **Create Order (quoted)**. The server recomputes from its own live configuration at redemption and never trusts a figure the token carries — a stale one yields **409 `QUOTE_STALE`** carrying the new breakdown, an expired one **409 `QUOTE_EXPIRED`** (research R10).

exec: const sum = b.fuelLineTotal + b.deliveryFee + b.serviceFee + b.tax;

request.description:
CLIENT — the real spec-005 ordering flow: **Quote Order** first, then submit the token it returned alongside the station it was quoted for.

The token is revalidated inside the existing creation transaction and the resulting `priceBreakdown` is persisted on the order, so the quote, the receipt and the invoice all show the same figures (FR-011e).

Returns **409 `QUOTE_STALE`** with the current breakdown if pricing moved since the quote — show the new total and re-confirm, never silently adopt either figure.

On `DEFERRED`/`CREDIT` terms no payment step follows (FR-014); `CREDIT` is refused over the available limit.

spec 008 FR-047. TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN (own transporter only — 404 for another carrier's order). The escape hatch for a driver who genuinely can't reach the platform to verify. Advances exactly the one outstanding stage — `409` if none is outstanding (can't skip ahead). Writes NO `VehicleVerification` record (research R10) — that omission is what keeps "overridden" structurally distinct from "verified": a customer's `vehicleVerified` stays `false` for a delivery that was only ever attested, never actually checked (FR-047d).
spec 008 FR-015. Pre-departure correction only — valid exactly at `ASSIGNED_TO_DRIVER` (once `LOADING` starts, the driver has already left for the depot).

Feature 009 FR-059-061/FR-067. TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN or SUPER_ADMIN. The transport dashboard's whole overview in one request — counts per stage group, drivers on duty, outstanding settlements. `from`/`to` (query params, ISO dates) default to the current month.

TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN (of the order's routed transporter). Order must be `ROUTED_TO_TRANSPORT`. Ranked list of that transporter's own available drivers by **proximity and availability only** — spec 008 moved capacity/grade capability to the tank, checked at tank selection instead. Each candidate carries `suggestedTruck` (their last-operated truck, derived from order history; `null` when they've never driven one or it's withdrawn/busy).

TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN (of the order's routed transporter). spec 008 FR-009: selection is sequential — driver, then truck, then tank (see **Trucks**/**Tanks** to create them first). Books all three atomically (txn) and stops at `ROUTED_TO_TRANSPORT` → `ASSIGNED_TO_DRIVER` — it no longer auto-advances to `IN_TRANSIT`; that now requires **Orders → Verify Vehicle** (departure), then the warehouse leg, then a second verification before **Orders → Confirm Loading** reaches `IN_TRANSIT`.

`409 TRUCK_UNAVAILABLE`/`TANK_UNAVAILABLE` (withdrawn or already committed), `409 TANK_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`/`TANK_GRADE_UNSUPPORTED` (chosen tank can't carry this order), `409 NO_WAREHOUSE_FOR_GRADE` (no in-service depot supplies the grade — checked before anything is booked), `409 ORDER_ALREADY_ASSIGNED` (a concurrent assignment already won). A refusal books nothing — all three resources are released together.

item.name: Trucks
item.description: spec 008 US1. TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN, scoped to their own company. A truck carries no capacity or fuel grade of its own — both moved to **Tanks** (research R3). `nfcCardUid`/`qrToken` are credentials, never returned by any read here (FR-042) — only the mint/rotate calls return a token, once, at mint time. Run **Create Truck** first, then **Pair NFC Card** or **Mint QR Token** so **Orders → Verify Vehicle** has something real to check against.

request.description: `model` is optional. `409 DUPLICATE_PLATE` if this company already has that plate.

`available=true` filters to `isActive` + no `activeOrderId`. The response's `fleetRegistered` distinguishes "nothing registered yet" from "registered but all busy" — both give an empty `items` array, so this flag is the only way to tell them apart (FR-043c).
Never touches `activeOrderId` (FR-008) — an in-progress delivery continues; this only blocks NEW assignments.

FR-005/SC-008: `409 CARD_ALREADY_PAIRED` (with `heldByPlateNumber`, feature 009 FR-050) if another truck already holds this card — both trucks are left unchanged. FR-036e: pairing a new card clears any previously minted `qrToken` on this truck.

The QR path for a device with no NFC (FR-036). This is one of only two responses that ever return a raw `qrToken` (FR-042) — copy it out now, since no read endpoint will show it again. Coexists with a paired card (FR-036d); minting doesn't disturb it.
Revoking a leaked code is a rotation, not an expiry wait (research R6). Same response shape as mint.
Revokes without minting a replacement — the truck falls back to card-only.

item.name: Tanks
item.description: spec 008 US1. TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN. The trailer — carries capacity and permitted grades (research R3), so the assignment guards (`TANK_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`/`TANK_GRADE_UNSUPPORTED`) validate THIS record, never the truck. A tank has no credential of any kind (FR-048c) — it's assigned, never verified.

request.description: `code` is unique **platform-wide**, not just within the company (FR-048b) — it reaches a driver's screen, so two tanks answering to one code would be ambiguous. `material` is `IRON` | `ALUMINIUM`, recorded as fact only — it never derives or constrains `fuelTypes` (FR-048g). `409 TANK_CODE_IN_USE` on a collision.
Same `fleetRegistered` distinction as **Trucks → List Trucks**.
Never touches `activeOrderId` — an in-progress delivery continues.

item.name: Warehouses
item.description: spec 008 US4. The one collection with **no tenant scoping at all** (research R1) — read by every authenticated role (a driver must be able to read the depot they're sent to), written only by SUPER_ADMIN. **Assign Driver** (see **Dispatch**) picks the nearest in-service warehouse supplying the order's grade automatically — create at least one here before assigning anything, or assignment fails with `NO_WAREHOUSE_FOR_GRADE`.

request.description: `externalRef` is optional — set it to make a later bulk load upsert onto this row instead of duplicating it (FR-035a).
Idempotent on `externalRef` → `{ created, updated }`. Re-running the national dataset updates existing rows rather than duplicating them.
Open to every authenticated role — shown here as DRIVER to make that explicit; any logged-in token works.
Affects only deliveries not yet assigned (FR-035e) — an order that already snapshotted this warehouse keeps showing it regardless.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN | TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN | CLIENT. Scoped by the multi-party plugin: a Fuel Company sees every invoice it issued (any method); a Transportation Company sees only DEFERRED invoices routed to them; a CLIENT sees only their own (spec 004 T072). Optional `?method=&state=` filters.
As **List Invoices**, scoped the same way, for a single invoice.

TRANSPORT_COMPANY_ADMIN (DEFERRED invoices only) or FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (CREDIT invoices only, swap the bearer token to `{{accessTokenCompanyAdmin}}`) — manual settlement for the two methods never confirmed by a payment-gateway webhook (spec 004 FR-022). `403` for a DIRECT invoice (settled only by **Payments (Webhooks)**) or the wrong role for the invoice's method. Idempotent: settling an already-SETTLED or VOIDed invoice is a no-op.

item.name: Stations
item.description:
A client's delivery destinations (spec 005 D2/US8). "Station" is the canonical term across the platform, the app and the specs.

Note the direction: a station **receives** fuel, it does not dispense it.

A client selects among their stations and marks favourites but may not add, rename or remove one — that is the fuel company's job, under **Users → Create Client Station**.

request.description:
CLIENT (spec 005 T014). The caller's own active stations, default first.

Scoped by `clientId` **on top of** the tenant plugin: company scoping alone is insufficient here, because two clients share a fuel company — this is the single likeliest place to introduce a cross-client leak.

Saves the first station to `{{stationId}}` for the quote and order requests.

CLIENT (spec 005 T107/FR-037). `isFavourite` is the **only** field a client may ever write on a station, and the DTO whitelists it alone — any other field is a 400 under `forbidNonWhitelisted`, which is what enforces "no rename" here (FR-036b).

The flip is persisted server-side, so it survives a restart and reaches the client's other devices.

Another client's station 404s — **including one in the same fuel company**.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (spec 005 T108). Every field optional.

`regionCode` and `governorateCode` must be updated **together** — validating the pairing needs both — and the governorate must belong to the region.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN. **204**, a soft delete — a withdrawn station stays readable on the historical orders that used it (FR-036c).

Deleting the client's last active station is refused with **409 `LAST_STATION`**; deleting the default promotes the next one, so the "exactly one default per client" invariant is held at the data layer by a partial unique index rather than assumed from ordering (Principle V).

item.name: Support
item.description:
Client support requests (spec 005 US9). Two states only — `SUBMITTED` and `ACKNOWLEDGED`. No threaded conversation, admin reply or resolution workflow is in scope (FR-039a).

A request routes to the administrators of the client's **own** fuel company through the existing notification path, never a second delivery mechanism (FR-038b).

request.description:
CLIENT (spec 005 T118). `topic` is one of `ORDER_ISSUE`, `PAYMENT`, `ACCOUNT`, `OTHER`. `message` is 1–2000 characters.

`orderId` is optional — when present the order is attached automatically, so the client never has to recite its number (FR-038). Attaching an order the client does not own 404s.

Raises a `SUPPORT_REQUEST_RAISED` notification to that fuel company's admins and to no other company (FR-038a).

CLIENT sees their own; FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN sees their company's whole set — same route, per-role query, with the tenant plugin scoping the admin view automatically.

This is how a client confirms a request was received and whether an administrator has acknowledged it (FR-039). Swap the bearer token to `{{accessTokenCompanyAdmin}}` for the admin view.

FUEL_COMPANY_ADMIN (spec 005 T118). `SUBMITTED → ACKNOWLEDGED`, one way — there is no reverse transition.

An admin of any other company gets a 404.
Any authenticated (company-scoped) user (FR-020). Stored under `sys_storge/{companyId}/`.
Same-company roles per purpose, or SUPER_ADMIN. Streams the file; 404 cross-tenant.
Own notifications only, for whichever role last logged in.
Own only.

query.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Omit for page one.

request.description:
CLIENT (spec 005 T074/US4). Cursor-paginated payment history, filtered to terminal outcomes, newest first.

`rawPayload` is projected away explicitly rather than left to be forgotten — it can carry gateway card metadata (Constitution Principle II).

A client sees only their own payments. Pass `cursor` from the previous page's `nextCursor`; `nextCursor: null` is the end of the list.

[public] Simulates the Sadad gateway confirming payment for `{{orderId}}`. The pre-request script builds the exact JSON body and signs it with `PAYMENT_SADAD_SECRET` (`paymentSadadSecret` variable) via HMAC-SHA256, matching `payments.service.ts`'s `verifySignature`. Run **Orders → Approve Order** first so `{{orderFinalPrice}}` is set.
[public] Same as the Sadad webhook but signed with `PAYMENT_MADA_SECRET` (`paymentMadaSecret` variable).
